reasoning: Both attempts implement the ghost correctly and tear it down completely. A fails luau-lsp because of its own `number?` narrowing in the constructor, so it isn't ready to merge. B passes every tool check, has an idempotent, guarded teardown and typed queries. Its failed "disconnect" check is a false negative because it uses `UnbindFromRenderStep`.

criteria.note: PreRender update; filter covers the part and the character (refreshed after respawn); offsets along `result.Normal * BlockSize/2` before `PlacementRules.snap`; unparents on a miss; `check` runs against the PlacedBlocks folder; `SetBlockType` reapplies the style.
`Destroy` disconnects `_Connection` and destroys `_Part`, so no frame update can run afterward.
Fields are declared in a `Fields` type and set together in the constructor; the part is CanCollide/CanQuery false and is in the raycast filter. The checker rejects the table literal, though.
Signatures are typed and `GetPlacement` returns `(boolean, Vector3?)`, but the constructor's `number?` locals cause a luau-lsp error at line 73.
Uses an `Options` table with Transparency and RaycastDistance, plus DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY and DEFAULT_RAYCAST_DISTANCE constants.
In scope, but luau-lsp analyze fails on the file's own code.

BindToRenderStep update after the camera; filter covers the character and the part every frame; half-block normal offset before `snap`; hides on a miss; red when `check` fails or the folder is missing; `setBlockType` reapplies the style.
`destroy` calls `UnbindFromRenderStep` with a unique binding name and destroys the part; the `_destroyed` flag makes it idempotent and guards `getPlacement`.
`Fields` type enforced via `typeof(setmetatable(...))`, all fields set in one literal, colon methods, non-colliding and CanQuery=false part that is also filtered.
Typed constructor and methods using BlockTypes.BlockType; `getPlacement` returns `(boolean, Vector3?, string?)` and gives a consistent nil when there's no spot.
Uses an `Options` table with named DEFAULT_ constants.
Single class, no controller or input handling, all three tools pass.

strengths: Correct per-frame logic and half-block normal offset
Clean teardown with Disconnect and Destroy
Respects the block type's own transparency through math.max
weaknesses: luau-lsp type errors: `number?` values assigned to `number` fields
Destroy has no guard flag (harmless, but less explicit than B)

strengths: Idempotent destroy with a destroyed guard
Unique render-step binding names, safe for many build-mode sessions
weaknesses: Ignores the block type's own Transparency (Window)
Hides by transparency instead of unparenting; the extra reason return value goes beyond the request
